name: Docker Engine
summary: A container engine that exposes a client-facing API through a daemon, delegates container execution to a runtime stack, and composes images and layered filesystems into isolated workloads.

features.name: Daemon API control plane
features.description: Docker Engine exposes a client API whose daemon owns image, container, network, and volume management and coordinates lifecycle operations.
benefits: Provides a stable client boundary across local and remote use
costs: The daemon is a shared availability and privilege boundary
API and daemon state must remain compatible

features.name: Layered runtime isolation stack
features.description: The Engine delegates low-level container execution through the containerd and OCI runtime stack, while Linux namespaces and cgroups provide process and resource isolation.
benefits: Separates lifecycle management from low-level execution
costs: Correctness depends on multiple runtime and kernel boundaries
Isolation behavior varies with host capabilities and configuration

features.name: Content-addressed image and filesystem layers
features.description: Docker images are composed from immutable layers and containers add a writable layer, allowing shared image content with per-container changes.
benefits: Separates distributable image state from container mutation
costs: Layer count and copy-on-write behavior affect performance
Deleting or changing data may not reduce lower-layer storage

mathematical_views.question: How do API requests transition image, container, network, and volume resources through lifecycle states?
assumptions: The daemon is the authority for modeled Engine resources
Runtime failures can leave transitions incomplete or failed

mathematical_views.question: How are daemon-managed containers mapped onto runtime, namespace, cgroup, and filesystem boundaries?
assumptions: The host kernel supplies the relevant isolation primitives
The model abstracts implementation details of individual OCI runtimes

mathematical_views.question: How does a writable container view refine shared immutable image layers?
assumptions: Image layers are treated as immutable inputs
The writable layer records container-specific changes
